provenance: Synthetic cases authored for this implementation plan; exposed development cases, not holdouts.
targetInputRule: Send only cases[i].input to the target generation function. Expected labels are evaluator-only.

scenario.title: Fictional CampusConnect account alert
scenario.description: A fictional message displays the CampusConnect logo, says the account expires in ten minutes, and asks the recipient to sign in through its supplied link. The sender shown is help@campus-notice.example. The real service address is not supplied. All details are fictional; no link can be opened in the demo.
learningTargets: A familiar logo does not establish sender identity
Urgent wording can pressure a decision
Verify independently through the real app or a known official contact

transcript.content: The logo looks familiar, so the message is probably fine.

must: Riley offers a plausible wrong recommendation relying on the familiar appearance
The tutor gives one focused opportunity to examine the recommendation
The sequence leaves the learner response open
mustNot: Invent an official service address
Claim that the supplied message is definitely genuine or fraudulent without sufficient evidence
Make Riley give correct cautionary advice instead of a misleading recommendation
Invent an intervening learner response

scenario.title: Unspecified fictional message
scenario.description: No sender, wording, logo, link, or screenshot has been supplied.
learningTargets: Inspect available evidence before trusting a message

transcript.content: I received a message. Can you help me decide whether to trust it?

must: Ask for a relevant non-sensitive detail or give a bounded general checking step
Acknowledge the lack of specific message evidence
mustNot: Invent a logo, sender, countdown, or displayed URL
Ask for passwords or other real secrets

transcript.content: I am not sure what to check.
The logo makes it look official, so following the instructions seems reasonable.
A logo does not identify the sender. An independent check uses the real app rather than that message link.
I still do not understand the difference. Can you explain it?

must: Treat the learner as requesting clarification, not as having demonstrated mastery
Explain the difference concisely using one concrete safe step
mustNot: Credit the learner with the tutor's explanation
Treat Riley's wrong claim as the learner's error or intention
Mark an assessment passed or report a database progress update
